domain_label: Movie Studio — Micro-Story Structure & Emotion for 15-60s Stitched Vertical Video
purpose: A method for the story decisions an expert makes when compressing narrative into a 15-60s vertical reel built from stitched 3-6s clips: winning the first 1-2 seconds against the retention cliff (Mosseri's 3-second hook framing carried as FACT, the Facebook 65/45 figure carried as FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-precision), mapping setup-escalation-payoff onto clip beats where every clip raises something, choosing hard-loop endings versus open-loop cliffhangers by format goal, knowing exactly what survives of 3-act / Freytag / hero-journey at reel scale (all tagged craft doctrine), and constructing luxury-persona hooks as aspiration snapshots legible at a muted glance — every empirical claim sourced honestly against the grounding file's FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags, never inventing an engagement statistic.
assumptions: no observed per-account retention dataset is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and every engagement figure is quoted from the grounding research file (story_and_emotion.md) with its honesty tag, never re-measured here

the Facebook 65%/45% 3-second-to-10s/30s figure traces to Facebook's own marketing communications via secondary citation only; the original Facebook IQ primary page was not retrievable, so the exact percentages are carried as FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-precision, never as audited fact

the '1.7 seconds to decide' and '60%+ 3-second hold gives 5-10x reach' figures circulate in marketing lore without a traceable primary controlled study; they are held as directional lore only and never cited as established

screenwriting structure (3-act, Freytag application, hero's journey, want/need, loops, tension-release) is human craft doctrine, not laboratory fact; it is tagged ESTIMATE / craft doctrine throughout, with only Freytag's five-part definition (Die Technik des Dramas, 1863) carried as FACT-of-definition

the target format is the owner-specified stitched reel: 3-6 second clips assembled into a 15-60s vertical whole for a classic-luxurious two-persona Instagram operation; silent autoplay is the default first exposure
exclusions: FACS action-unit vocabulary and facial-expression prompting mechanics (they belong to the expression/prompting knowledge, not the story-beat layer; this KB only consumes 'restraint reads as class' as a hook/beat direction)
camera moves, stitch-transition grammar, and edit-rhythm mechanics (the camera & editing research file's domain; this KB names WHICH beat a transition must serve, not how to shoot it)
score selection, voice generation, and WPM delivery direction (the audio/soundtrack domain; this KB only marks where tension-release and the sound-on bonus land)
posting cadence, ranking-signal optimization, and platform-algorithm tactics beyond the story-side consequence that shareable awe drives sends (media-manager domain)

Higgsfield model names, ids, parameters, durations, or aspect-ratio settings — none are quoted here because this KB carries story structure only, and tool surface facts come solely from higgsfield_surface.md in the KBs that need them
any guidance for evoking a specific real person while concealing the face (the likeness closed lane stays closed); celebrity-adjacency legal boundaries live in the legal research file
restating the 5-10x hold-rate lore, the 1.7-second decision figure, or any other unverified engagement statistic as established fact

competency_questions.question: What exactly does the retention evidence say about the first seconds of a reel, and how must the Facebook 65/45 figure be carried?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states Mosseri publicly frames the first three seconds as the hook with early retention consistent across videos and differentiation after ~3s [FACT], quotes the Facebook 65%-to-10s / 45%-to-30s figure as FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-precision because the Facebook IQ primary page is not retrievable, and rejects the 1.7s and 5-10x figures as untraceable lore

competency_questions.question: What makes a compliant frame-one hook for a reel that must survive a sub-2-second swipe decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer requires opening on the most visually arresting frame with motion in frame one, front-loading the promise so the world is legible within 1-2s even muted, and bans slow builds, logo intros, and establishing pans that pay off later, tagging these as craft doctrine

competency_questions.question: How does a luxury-persona hook differ from a generic hook?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer defines the hook frame as an aspiration snapshot — status legible at a glance (the car door opening, the penthouse reveal, the tailored silhouette turning to camera) — with restraint over flash, and keeps motion-in-frame-one and no-slow-build intact

competency_questions.question: How are stitched 3-6s clips mapped onto the compressed 4-part shape, and how short must the setup be?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer maps each clip to a beat of Hook, Setup, Escalation, Payoff/Loop rather than treating the reel as one scene, and confines setup to roughly clips 1-2 (seconds ~2-8) establishing who/where/what-tension with no long runway

competency_questions.question: What must every middle clip in the stitch do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states each stitched clip must raise something — a bigger location, a wardrobe change, rising musical intensity, an accelerating edit — with the stitch transitions carrying the escalation energy, and names the sagging-middle failure when a clip repeats instead of raises

competency_questions.question: Why must the payoff be visual, and what must it deliver?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states the payoff must deliver the exact promise the hook made (destination reveal, final look, quote punchline, music drop) and must be visual not spoken because autoplay is muted, citing the ~85% Digiday figure as FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality (2016, publisher-reported)

competency_questions.question: What are the hard-loop mechanics and what is the evidence status of looping as a tactic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states seamless looping is a documented watch-time tactic (clean loops multiply watch time per view via unnoticed rewatch, aligning with Mosseri's watch-time signal) [FACT], gives the mechanics — match last frame composition/motion/lighting to the first, end on continuing motion, loop the audio — and flags the 7-10s optimal-loop-length claim as marketing-blog directional only

competency_questions.question: When does an open-loop cliffhanger beat a hard loop, and who decides?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states the hard loop optimizes rewatch/watch-time while the open loop (an unresolved beat, a numbered part) optimizes comments and follows, and gives the selection rule: choose per format goal — loopable atmospheric formats take the hard loop, series formats with a genuine next installment take the open loop

competency_questions.question: What survives of 3-act structure, Freytag's pyramid, and the hero's journey at reel scale, and how is that knowledge tagged?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer collapses 3-act to Hook+Setup / Escalation / Payoff-Loop with act-2 conflict surviving only as tension, states Freytag's five parts as FACT-of-definition (1863) but cuts falling action and denouement entirely — a rising line that cuts or loops at the climax — and moves the hero's journey to series level where one beat can be one reel; all application tagged ESTIMATE / craft doctrine

competency_questions.question: How does the information-gap theory of curiosity shape reel openings and endings?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer cites Loewenstein (1994, Psychological Bulletin) — curiosity as cognitively induced deprivation from a perceived, fillable knowledge gap [FACT] — and applies it: open on a gap, withhold the fill until the payoff, use the open loop as a deliberately unfilled gap, and never over-tease into clickbait that breeds distrust

competency_questions.question: Which emotional registers drive sharing and held attention, and how do they map onto luxury content?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer cites Berger & Milkman (2012, JMR) — high-arousal emotions (awe positively; anger/anxiety negatively) are more viral while low-arousal sadness is less viral [FACT] — positions luxury reveals as awe machines, requires a tension-release build so the reel does not read as a slideshow, and includes one aspiration this-could-be-you beat (craft doctrine, not a basic emotion)

competency_questions.question: How do want-versus-need and recurring formats carry a narrative arc across posts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states the want (visible pursuit) is shown per reel while the need (the value the brand stands for) is revealed across the series [craft doctrine], and names the recurring formats — come-with-me POV arrival, transformation/reveal, quote-over-cinematic, a-day-a-place, dual-persona interplay — with numbered open loops converting curiosity into follows

glossary.definition: The first ~3 seconds of a reel where, per Adam Mosseri's public framing, the hook lives: early-second retention is remarkably consistent across videos regardless of eventual performance, and differentiation happens after the ~3-second mark where strong videos hold and weak ones drop sharply [FACT — Mosseri public statements via secondary aggregation, sources 8/9 of the grounding file].

The much-cited claim that 65% of people who watch the first 3 seconds of a video watch at least 10 seconds and 45% continue to 30 seconds; it traces to Facebook's own marketing communications, but the original Facebook IQ primary page is not directly retrievable, so the exact percentages are carried as FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-precision — Facebook said it, the methodology cannot be audited.

The luxury-persona hook frame: a single image in which status is legible at a glance — the car door opening, the penthouse reveal, the tailored silhouette turning to camera — with motion in frame one and no slow build [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

An ending engineered so the last frame flows invisibly back into the first (matched composition, motion, lighting; ending on continuing motion, not a hard stop) so viewers rewatch without noticing; a documented watch-time tactic aligned with watch-time ranking signals [FACT for the tactic; the 7-10s optimal length claim is marketing-blog directional only].

An ending on a deliberately unresolved beat — a part-2 promise, an unfilled curiosity gap — that trades rewatch for comments and follows; per Loewenstein's information-gap theory, the unfilled gap sustains curiosity across posts [craft application of a FACT-grounded mechanism].

The compression discipline for stitched reels: each 3-6s clip is assigned one beat of the 4-part shape Hook, Setup, Escalation, Payoff/Loop, rather than treating the 15-60s whole as one continuous scene [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

The rule that every middle clip must raise something — a bigger location, a wardrobe change, rising musical intensity, an accelerating edit — with the stitch transitions themselves carrying the escalation energy; a clip that merely repeats produces the sagging middle [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

The requirement that the whole story reads with sound off, because feed video autoplays muted; the much-cited ~85%-watched-without-sound figure is publisher-reported 2016 Digiday data (FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality), but the load-bearing implication — carry meaning in visuals and on-screen text, treat audio as a bonus — stands independent of the exact percentage.

The single biggest structural difference from long-form: of Freytag's five parts (exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, denouement — Die Technik des Dramas, 1863 [FACT-of-definition]), falling action and denouement essentially do not survive at reel scale; the compressed reel is a rising line that cuts to black or loops at the climax [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

Craft doctrine: the want is the external plot-driving pursuit shown in each reel (destination, acquisition, achievement); the need is the internal value the brand stands for (freedom, self-mastery, taste) revealed across the series — the need is what makes an audience bond rather than just envy [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, No Film School / Go Into The Story framing].

nodes.definition: Impose the compression frame the whole KB reasons in: the owner-specified reel is 3-6 second clips stitched into a 15-60s whole, and that constraint forces the compressed 4-part shape Hook, Setup, Escalation, Payoff/Loop. The expert move is to map each stitched clip to exactly one beat rather than treating the reel as one continuous scene — the clip boundary IS the beat boundary, so clip count budgets the story (a 15s reel of 4-5s clips carries only 3-4 beats; a 60s reel carries 10+ and must ladder them). This mapping is what makes every downstream decision computable: which clip is the hook frame, how many clips setup may consume, which clips must escalate, and which clip lands the payoff [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine throughout — this is compression discipline, not laboratory fact].

nodes.definition: Enforce the muted-first-exposure constraint on every story decision. FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality: the much-cited figure that ~85% of Facebook video is watched without sound comes from Digiday (Sahil Patel, May 17 2016) reporting publisher-specific ranges (LittleThings ~85%, Mic ~85% of 30s views, MEC clients ~85-90%) — publishers said it, it is a 2016 publisher-reported number, not a current platform-measured universal. The load-bearing implication is independent of the exact percentage: feed video autoplays muted, so a large majority of first exposures are silent and the story must be fully legible with the sound off. Consequences: carry meaning in expression, body language, action, environment, and on-screen text; caption anything spoken; use a bold text hook in seconds 0-2 as a layer that works when audio does not play; design the sound-on moment (score drop, whispered line) as a bonus for the minority who unmute, never a dependency. Show-not-tell follows: depict behavior instead of captioning emotion labels [craft doctrine].

the sound-off legibility requirement and its design consequences
text-hook layering and captioning of spoken content
excluded: voice-delivery and score direction (audio file's domain)

cons.claim: Designing sound-off-first can flatten reels whose best weapon is audio, and the 85% anchor is a 2016 publisher figure that may misstate current behavior

nodes.definition: Construct the opening 1-2 seconds to survive the swipe decision the retention evidence locates there. The patterns [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, grounding sources 8 and 11]: open on the most visually arresting frame, never a slow build — no logo intro, no establishing pan that pays off later; front-load the promise so the viewer knows within 1-2 seconds what world they are in (luxury, travel, transformation) even muted; put motion in frame one — a moving subject, a reveal, a whip-in — because static openings bleed viewers. The hook is a promise the payoff must later honor, so hook construction and payoff design are one contract written at two ends of the reel. Because autoplay is muted, the hook must also work as pure image plus optional text layer — a spoken opening line is not a hook.

the hook-as-promise contract with the payoff
muted operability of the hook
excluded: luxury-register specialization of the hook (its own node)

nodes.definition: Specialize the hook for the classic-luxurious persona register: the hook frame is an aspiration snapshot — status legible at a glance, muted, in under two seconds. Grounding-file examples: the car door opening, the penthouse reveal, the tailored silhouette turning to camera [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The general hook rules stay binding — motion in frame one, no slow build — but the arrest comes from aspiration rather than shock: the frame must let the viewer instantly project a desired self into the scene. The register is quiet luxury: texture, cut, and setting over loud branding, restraint over flash — a hook that screams reads as trying-too-hard and breaks the persona. The persona's face-and-wardrobe consistency is what makes the snapshot read as one ongoing world rather than stock footage; the mechanics of that consistency live in the character/wardrobe domain, but the hook must be composed to display it.

nodes.definition: Compress the setup beat to roughly clips 1-2 (seconds ~2-8): establish who, where, and what-tension — the persona grounded in a place and a mood — in one to two short clips, because the compressed form cannot afford a long runway [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The setup inherits whatever the hook already established: if the hook frame named the world, setup only needs to add the tension (where are we going, what changes, what is about to happen). Setup never repeats the hook's information — repetition here is the first place a reel goes slack. In the shortest reels (15s, 3-4 clips) setup collapses entirely into the hook clip, and the plan must acknowledge that collapse explicitly rather than silently spending a scarce clip re-establishing.

inheritance from the hook and the no-repetition rule

excluded: the escalation content that follows (its own node)

nodes.definition: Design the middle clips as a ladder where each stitched clip raises something: a bigger location, a wardrobe change, a rising musical intensity, an accelerating edit [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The stitch transitions themselves — match cut, whip pan, outfit-change snap — carry the escalation energy (their camera grammar lives in the camera/editing file; this KB assigns what each transition must accomplish narratively). The ladder must be planned as an ordered sequence of raises before production, because raises are relative: a clip only escalates if it exceeds the previous clip on some legible axis. A clip that merely varies (same scale, new angle) is a rung that holds instead of raises — one is tolerable as breath, two in a row is the sagging middle that bleeds the post-hook retention Mosseri says differentiates strong videos. Longer reels need more rungs, so the 45-60s band demands either a deeper location/wardrobe budget or a second escalation axis (edit pace, music) layered on the first.

transitions as carriers of escalation energy

excluded: transition camera grammar (camera/editing file)

nodes.definition: Land the final clip as the delivery of the exact promise the hook made: the destination reveal, the final look, the quote punchline, the drop in the music [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. Two binding rules. First, promise-match: the payoff must fill the specific gap the hook opened — a hook promising a penthouse cannot pay off with a car, however beautiful; mismatch is experienced as clickbait and, per the curiosity-gap grounding, unfilled or falsely filled gaps breed distrust. Second, silent operability: because autoplay is muted, the payoff must be visual — or carried by on-screen text — never a spoken line alone; the music drop version of a payoff needs a visual event at the same beat so the muted majority still receives the landing. The payoff should be the top rung of the escalation ladder: the one raise the middle clips never exceeded.

visual/text delivery under muted autoplay
payoff as the ladder's top rung
excluded: the loop or cliffhanger engineered after the payoff (their own nodes)
score-drop construction (audio file)

pros.claim: A promise-matched visual payoff converts the hook's borrowed attention into satisfaction, the precondition for rewatch, share, and follow
pros.example: a where-does-this-road-go hook paying off on the cliff-edge villa reveal at golden hour, the reel's largest scale

cons.claim: Reserving the biggest moment for the end risks the whole investment on viewers who survive the middle — a weak ladder starves the payoff of witnesses
cons.example: a spectacular final reveal that most viewers never reach because clips three and four held instead of raised

nodes.definition: Engineer the hard-loop ending: design the final frame to flow back into the first so the restart is invisible. FACT (grounding source 10): seamless looping is a documented watch-time tactic — a clean loop multiplies watch time per view because viewers rewatch without noticing, and high completion/replay signals push distribution, aligning with Mosseri's stated watch-time ranking signal. Mechanics [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: match the last frame's composition, motion, and lighting to the first; end on continuing motion rather than a hard stop; if audio is used, pick or edit audio that also loops cleanly. Canonical persona moves: the subject re-enters the same doorway, the same turn-to-camera. The suggested 7-10s loop length for maximum replay comes from a marketing blog, not a platform study — directional only, never cited as fact. Hard looping is a two-ended design constraint: the first frame must be composed with its own return in mind, so the loop decision must be made before the hook is shot, not after the payoff.

included: last-frame-to-first-frame matching on composition/motion/lighting
end-on-continuing-motion and audio-loop hygiene
the watch-time rationale and the 7-10s caveat
excluded: when to choose the loop over a cliffhanger (selection node)
loop-friendly music editing mechanics (audio file)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: replay-rate evidence or a real loop-length study changes when and how hard loops are engineered

pros.claim: An invisible loop converts one viewer into multiple watch-throughs without asking anything of them, feeding the watch-time signal directly

nodes.definition: Engineer the open-loop ending: close the reel on a deliberately unresolved beat — a part-2 promise, an interrupted approach, a door not yet opened — that drives comments and follows rather than rewatch [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, grounding section 1.3 and 8.2]. Its mechanism is the curiosity gap left deliberately unfilled: per Loewenstein's information-gap theory the viewer is left in cognitively induced deprivation that the NEXT post promises to relieve, converting single-view curiosity into subscription. Numbered series markers (Part 1 of..., Location 3 of 7) make the promise explicit and give a reason to follow. Two integrity rules: the reel must still deliver its own hook's promise before opening the next gap (an open loop is not an excuse for a missing payoff), and the promised continuation must actually be produced — a part 2 that never posts is the account-scale version of clickbait and burns the trust the series depends on.

nodes.definition: Decide the ending mode per reel from the format's goal, because the two modes optimize different and partly exclusive outcomes [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The hard loop maximizes watch time per view via invisible rewatch — it wins for atmospheric, self-contained formats (quote-over-cinematic, a-day-a-place mood pieces) where the reel is its own destination and composition can return to frame one. The open loop maximizes comments and follows via an unfilled gap — it wins for journey and transformation formats with a genuine next installment, and for series builds where subscription is the goal. Selection inputs: does the format's payoff permit a return to frame one (one-way reveals cannot hard-loop honestly); does a continuation actually exist; is the account currently optimizing reach-per-post (loop) or audience growth (open loop). The decision must be made at planning time because the hard loop constrains the hook composition and the open loop obligates a future post — retrofitting either is rework.

nodes.definition: Compress 3-act structure honestly [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine throughout]: Setup - Confrontation - Resolution collapses at reel scale to Hook+Setup (Act 1), Escalation (Act 2), Payoff/Loop (Act 3). The act-2 confrontation is the thinnest survivor: a 20s reel rarely has room for genuine plot conflict, so confrontation survives only as TENSION — a curiosity gap, rising stakes, will-they-arrive — not as an obstacle-and-struggle sequence. The expert use of this node is negative as much as positive: knowing the mapping stops a writer importing long-form act machinery (midpoint reversals, B-stories, character-versus-character conflict) that the clip budget cannot carry, while keeping the one thing 3-act genuinely contributes at this scale — the discipline that something must be at stake between the opening and the landing.

nodes.definition: Apply Freytag with the back half amputated. FACT-of-definition: Gustav Freytag, Die Technik des Dramas (1863), names five parts — exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, denouement — with tension rising to a mid-point climax then falling to resolution. ESTIMATE / craft doctrine for the reel-scale mapping: exposition is the hook frame; rising action is the escalation clips; climax is the payoff; falling action and denouement essentially do not survive, because a 15-30s reel cannot afford a wind-down. The compressed reel is a rising line that cuts to black — or loops — AT the climax, not after it. This is the single biggest structural difference from long-form: you cut the entire back half of Freytag. The node's working rule: any clip planned after the payoff must justify itself as loop engineering or open-loop gap, never as resolution — resolution is a long-form luxury the format does not possess.

the reel mapping and the falling-action/denouement cut
the no-clip-after-the-payoff-except-loop-or-gap rule
excluded: stage-drama Freytag scholarship

nodes.definition: Relocate the hero's journey to the correct altitude [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: the Campbell/Vogler monomyth (ordinary world, call, threshold, trials, reward, return) is far too long for one reel. What survives: (a) a single beat can BE a reel — the threshold crossing is the car pulling out of the gate; the reward is the summit reveal — so the monomyth becomes a menu of reel-sized moments; (b) the full arc spreads across a SERIES, where each post is one beat and the account is the journey. The expert rule: treat the monomyth as a series-level skeleton, never a per-reel one. Per-reel it produces overstuffed plans that try to cross a threshold, endure trials, and return home in 25 seconds; series-level it gives the account a spine — early posts establish the aspirational world, a mid-series turn, later posts pay off the transformation — that disconnected flexes lack.

the series-level skeleton use
the ban on per-reel full arcs
excluded: want/need value revelation (its own node)

nodes.definition: Engineer curiosity from its actual mechanism. FACT: Loewenstein (1994), The Psychology of Curiosity, Psychological Bulletin 116(1):75-98, gives the information-gap theory — curiosity is a form of cognitively induced deprivation arising from a perceived gap between what one knows and wants to know, and its intensity rises with how fillable the gap feels. Application [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: open the reel on a gap (what is behind this door, where does this road go, what happens at the end) and withhold the fill until the payoff; the gap must feel fillable within this reel, or across the series for open loops. Two integrity constraints: never over-tease — clickbait that never fills breeds distrust and poisons the account's future gaps; and size the gap to the fill — a gap bigger than its payoff is experienced as betrayal even when technically filled. The curiosity gap is the story-side mechanism behind both the hook's promise and the open-loop ending.

gap-opening, withheld-fill, and gap-to-fill sizing
the anti-clickbait integrity constraints
excluded: the open-loop ending construction (its own node)
caption copywriting mechanics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audience trust signals or gap-vs-direct performance data recalibrate how aggressively gaps are opened

pros.claim: Grounding hooks in the information-gap mechanism gives a principled generator for openings instead of a swipe-file of tricks
pros.example: converting a flat location reel into a where-does-this-corridor-lead structure by hiding the destination the drone shot revealed in second one

cons.claim: Gap-driven openings pull toward withholding exactly the arresting imagery the hook rule wants shown, and overuse trains the audience to expect manipulation
cons.example: an account whose every reel opens on a concealed doorway until the format itself becomes the predictable non-surprise

failure_modes: opening a gap the reel never fills (clickbait)
a gap so oblique the viewer never perceives it (no deprivation, no curiosity)

nodes.definition: Design the emotional register for sharing from the fetched evidence. FACT: Berger & Milkman (2012), Journal of Marketing Research, analyzing all New York Times articles over ~3 months, found content evoking high-arousal emotions is more viral — positive awe, and negative anger and anxiety — while low-arousal deactivating emotions like sadness are less viral; positive content is generally more viral than negative, but AROUSAL is the mechanism, holding controlling for surprise, interest, usefulness, and placement. Application [ESTIMATE grounded in that FACT]: luxury travel, architecture, and nature reels are awe machines — sweeping reveals, scale, grandeur — and awe sits in exactly the sharable quadrant, both aspirational and high-arousal. So the payoff beat should be built for awe (scale and reveal) whenever the format allows, and story design should optimize for the share/send as its distribution-side outcome — the register where story craft and reach mechanics agree. The negative high-arousal lane (anger, anxiety) is viral but off-register for a classic-luxury persona and is not used.

awe as the luxury payoff register
declining the negative-arousal lane for this persona
excluded: sends-per-reach ranking tactics (media-manager domain)
reveal-shot camera grammar (camera/editing file)

nodes.definition: Install the tension-release engine that separates a story from a slideshow [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: build a small tension — a rising musical swell, an unfinished motion, an approaching reveal — and release it on the payoff. In stitched reels the edit rhythm and score carry this build (their mechanics live in the camera/editing and audio files; this KB specifies where the build starts, how long it holds, and which beat releases it). The story-side rules: tension must begin no later than the setup's what-tension element and rise monotonically with the escalation ladder; the release must coincide with the payoff beat, not straggle after it; and a reel with no tension-release reads as a slideshow — the universal engine of held attention is absent, however beautiful the clips. Because most viewing is muted, at least one tension carrier must be visual (unfinished motion, approach, withheld reveal), with the score swell as reinforcement, not the sole carrier.

the slideshow failure diagnosis
excluded: score composition and edit-rhythm mechanics (audio and camera files)

nodes.definition: Place the aspiration beat [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: aspiration is not one of the classic basic emotions; it operates as desired-self projection — the viewer imagines themselves in the persona's position. Levers: proximity (first-person POV shots, the come-with-me framing), attainability signaling (the lifestyle felt as reachable, not merely observed), and identity cues matching the target audience's ideal self. The story-side rule this KB owns: every reel should contain at least one this-could-be-you moment — a beat composed so the viewer occupies the persona's position rather than watching it from outside. The deeper psychology of attraction and audience identity is the media-manager/psychology file's domain; here aspiration is a BEAT with a slot in the clip plan, most naturally inside the escalation (a POV clip among the third-person raises) or as the texture of the payoff.

nodes.definition: Split the persona's story fuel across altitudes [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, No Film School and Go Into The Story framing]: the WANT is the external, conscious, plot-driving goal; the NEED is the internal, often unconscious value — want drives plot, need drives the arc. In a persona operation this maps to: the want is the visible pursuit each reel shows (the destination, the acquisition, the achievement); the need is the underlying value the brand stands for (freedom, self-mastery, taste) revealed ACROSS the series, never stated in one post. Per-reel you show the want; across posts you reveal the need. This is what keeps content from being pure flex — the need is what makes an audience bond rather than just envy. Practically: every reel plan names its want; the series plan names the need and tracks which posts have advanced its revelation; a quarter of pure want-posts with no need progression is a flex account, not a story.

nodes.definition: Operate a small set of named recurring formats the personas cycle through, because recurring formats build viewer expectation and lower production cost [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The grounded starting set: come-with-me (first-person POV arrival with an awe payoff), transformation/reveal (before-to-after outfit or plain-to-destination on the escalation-then-payoff shape), quote-over-cinematic (a motivational line as text over a luxury clip — the owner's stated pillar, silent-autoplay native), a-day-a-place (episodic slice-of-life with mystery/aloofness maintained), and dual-persona interplay (the male and female personas in complementary or paired formats — a recurring relational thread). Each format carries defaults: its ending mode, its emotional register, its beat template — so a format choice pre-answers most per-reel decisions. Numbered open loops (Part 1 of..., Location 3 of 7) attach to journey formats to convert curiosity into follows. The format grid is where all the per-reel doctrine gets amortized into a repeatable production system.

edges.why_related: the gap mechanism wants to withhold the reveal for as long as possible while the payoff owes complete delivery — over-withholding becomes clickbait, over-delivering kills curiosity early

conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide per format at planning time via ENDING_MODE_SELECTION; atmospheric self-contained formats loop, journey/series formats with real continuations open

conflict_axes.name: arrest vs grounding
conflict_axes.description: Frame one wants maximal visual arrest to survive the swipe; the story wants early grounding (who, where, tension). Both compete for the same first seconds and the compressed form cannot fully serve both.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: arrest wins the first 1-2 seconds absolutely; grounding inherits the hook's information and takes only the remainder of clips 1-2

conflict_axes.name: withholding vs delivery
conflict_axes.description: The curiosity gap runs on withheld information, but withheld too long or filled too small it becomes clickbait that burns trust; delivered too early it kills the reason to keep watching.
poles: withhold the fill to sustain curiosity
deliver the promise completely and on time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: withholding may extend through the escalation but every gap is filled at the payoff unless a declared open loop with a scheduled continuation takes the debt

conflict_axes.name: release vs seam
conflict_axes.description: Tension wants a felt release landing on the payoff; the hard loop wants continuing motion through the final frame into frame one. A dead-stop landing breaks the seam; a seamless glide can flatten the climax.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: on looped reels, carry the release in the reveal's visual content at peak scale while motion continues; formats that need a full-stop landing should not be hard-looped

conflict_axes.name: awe grandeur vs aspiration proximity
conflict_axes.description: Awe is delivered by third-person scale observed from outside; aspiration is delivered by first-person occupancy felt from inside. The same beat cannot be maximally both, yet luxury content needs both registers.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: distribute across beats: awe owns the payoff reveal, the aspiration POV beat lives in the escalation or the hook snapshot

conflict_axes.name: text legibility vs quiet register
conflict_axes.description: Muted autoplay favors a bold text-hook layer; the patrician quiet-luxury register favors clean restrained frames. Loud text on an understated image breaks the register that defines the persona.
poles: bold text layer for the muted majority
clean frame for the quiet-luxury register
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: legibility wins whenever the image alone cannot name the world; the text is then styled with typographic restraint so it serves the register instead of shouting over it

conflict_axes.name: doctrine vs evidence
conflict_axes.description: Most of this KB is craft doctrine (structure collapses, hook patterns, loops) while a minority is fetched fact (Mosseri framing, Loewenstein, Berger & Milkman). Doctrine tempts over-claiming as fact; evidence tempts over-generalizing from other media (2012 article sharing, 2016 sound data) to today's reels.
poles: treat craft doctrine as established fact
restrict claims to the fetched evidence's actual scope
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry every claim at its tag: FACT with source, FACT-of-attribution with caveat, ESTIMATE/craft doctrine named as such; when doctrine and measured account data disagree, the account data wins

conflict_axes.name: per-reel completeness vs series arc
conflict_axes.description: Every reel must stand alone for the cold unordered feed audience, yet the account's real narrative (the monomyth arc, the need's revelation) lives across posts and needs reels to carry series weight.
poles: series beats that assume prior posts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: standalone hook/payoff discipline is never sacrificed; series meaning rides on top as an optional deeper layer for followers, and any reel that fails cold-viewer checks is rejected regardless of its arc role

edge_cases.description: A brief or caption is about to cite the 1.7-second decision figure or the 60%+ hold gives 5-10x reach claim as established fact, when neither traces to a primary controlled study
edge_cases.trigger: any retention statistic appears in planning output without a source tag from the grounding file
edge_cases.mitigation: strike or re-tag as directional marketing lore; only the Mosseri 3-second framing (FACT) and the tagged 65/45 attribution may be cited, each with its caveat

edge_cases.description: The Facebook 65/45 figure hardens into audited platform truth as it moves between documents, because the FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-precision tag gets dropped in transit — the primary Facebook IQ page remains unretrievable, which is the named blocker on auditing it
edge_cases.trigger: the 65/45 percentages appear anywhere without the attribution-only caveat
edge_cases.mitigation: re-attach the caveat at every citation; the blocker (Facebook IQ primary page not retrievable) is carried openly and the figure is never load-bearing on its precision

edge_cases.description: A reel is produced as one continuous 20s take rather than stitched 3-6s clips, so clip boundaries no longer mark beat boundaries and the beat-per-clip discipline has nothing to attach to
edge_cases.trigger: a format or model output delivers a single continuous shot instead of a stitch
edge_cases.mitigation: map beats to time windows instead of cuts and demand in-shot raises (camera approach, light change, subject action); flag that transition-carried escalation is unavailable

edge_cases.description: At the 15s minimum with 3-4 clips, there is no room for a separate setup beat — setup must collapse into the hook clip or the reel loses an escalation rung
edge_cases.trigger: reel length 15-20s with clip count at or below four
edge_cases.mitigation: declare the collapse explicitly: the hook clip carries who/where/tension in its composition, clips 2-3 escalate, the final clip pays off; never spend a scarce clip re-establishing

edge_cases.description: At the 60s maximum the escalation ladder runs out of legible raises — locations and wardrobe exhaust before the clips do, and the middle sags exactly where post-3s differentiation happens
edge_cases.trigger: reel plans above ~45s where consecutive middle clips hold rather than raise
edge_cases.mitigation: layer a second escalation axis (edit pace, music intensity, motion energy) over the exhausted first, or cut the reel shorter — a tight 30s beats a sagging 60s

edge_cases.description: An open-loop reel publishes its part-1 promise but the continuation never posts, converting the borrowed curiosity into account-scale clickbait and comment-section distrust
edge_cases.trigger: an open-loop ending publishes without a continuation slot in the series plan, or the slotted continuation slips past its window
edge_cases.mitigation: gate open-loop publishing on an existing continuation slot; if a continuation dies after publishing, close the loop cheaply (a follow-up or caption resolution) rather than leaving the debt open

edge_cases.description: A destination-reveal payoff is one-way — the summit, the opened door — and cannot return to frame one, so a hard loop would produce a visible teleport at the seam
edge_cases.trigger: the chosen format's payoff changes location, time, or state irreversibly relative to frame one
edge_cases.mitigation: select the open loop or a plain ending instead; alternatively design a motion-loop variant where a repeating action (the turn, the stride) loops within the destination rather than back to the origin

edge_cases.description: The payoff is a spoken punchline and the muted majority receives a reel that visibly ends but delivers nothing
edge_cases.trigger: any payoff beat whose content exists only in the audio track
edge_cases.mitigation: add the visual or on-screen-text carrier for the same beat; the spoken version remains as the sound-on bonus

edge_cases.description: The 7-10s optimal-loop-length claim gets treated as a platform finding when its only source is a marketing blog, skewing format lengths toward very short loops
edge_cases.trigger: loop-length guidance appears in planning with source-free confidence
edge_cases.mitigation: tag the figure directional-only; choose loop length from the format's content needs and test against the account's own replay data when available

edge_cases.description: A planner attempts the full hero's journey inside one reel — ordinary world, call, threshold, trials, reward, return in 25 seconds — producing an overstuffed plan where no beat lands
edge_cases.trigger: a single-reel plan containing more than one monomyth beat or more beats than clips
edge_cases.mitigation: cut to one monomyth beat per reel and move the arc to the series plan; the beat count must fit the clip count

edge_cases.description: A curiosity-gap hook overpromises and the payoff, though present, is smaller than the tease — the gap is technically filled but the viewer experiences betrayal and the account's future gaps weaken
edge_cases.trigger: review finds the hook's implied promise exceeds what the final clip actually shows
edge_cases.mitigation: resize one end of the contract: soften the tease or upgrade the payoff clip; ship only when the fill is proportionate to the gap

workflow.action: Confirm the evidence framing and its honesty tags before any creative work
workflow.description: Restate what may be claimed: Mosseri 3-second hook framing as FACT, the 65/45 figure as attribution-only, the 1.7s/5-10x lore excluded; set the working target that the hook must survive a sub-2-second muted swipe
workflow.artifact: an evidence sheet with each retention claim at its tagged strength
workflow.gate: no untagged or lore-grade statistic appears anywhere in the plan

workflow.action: Choose the format from the series grid and slot the reel in the arc
workflow.description: Pick one named format (come-with-me, transformation, quote-over-cinematic, a-day-a-place, dual-persona) and record which want this reel shows and whether it advances the need
workflow.artifact: a format selection with the reel's want named and its series-arc contribution marked
workflow.gate: the reel maps to a documented format or is an explicit experiment; the want is named

workflow.action: Fix the ending mode before anything is composed
workflow.description: Decide hard loop vs open loop from the format's default and this reel's material: can the payoff return to frame one, does a continuation slot exist, is the goal reach or follows
workflow.artifact: a recorded ending-mode decision with its justification
workflow.gate: the decision predates hook composition; open loops have an existing continuation slot

workflow.action: Budget the clips against the four beats
workflow.description: From the reel length and 3-6s clip duration, allocate each clip exactly one beat: hook, setup (possibly collapsed), escalation rungs, payoff/loop
workflow.gate: beat count fits clip count; every clip has exactly one named beat

workflow.action: Design the hook frame as an aspiration snapshot
workflow.description: Compose frame one with motion, glance-legible status in the quiet-luxury register, the promise front-loaded, and — if the ending is a hard loop — the return composition planned in
workflow.artifact: the hook-frame direction: subject, motion, register, promise
workflow.gate: a cold viewer names the world within 2 seconds muted; no slow build, no loud branding

workflow.action: Compress the setup into at most two clips
workflow.description: Establish who/where/what-tension in clips 1-2 (seconds ~2-8), inheriting the hook's information; declare the collapse when the length band forces it
workflow.artifact: the setup beat content with its tension named
workflow.gate: setup ends by ~8s and repeats nothing the hook showed; a tension exists for the ladder to raise

workflow.action: Plan the escalation ladder as ordered raises
workflow.description: List each middle clip with its raise axis (location scale, wardrobe, pace, music) strictly exceeding the previous clip, reserving the top raise for the payoff
workflow.artifact: the ordered ladder with a named raise per clip
workflow.gate: no two consecutive holds; no mid-ladder raise exceeds the payoff

workflow.action: Design the visual payoff that fills the hook's promise
workflow.description: Land the promised reveal/look/punchline as the ladder's top rung, carried visually or by on-screen text, with the awe register (scale, reveal) where the format allows
workflow.artifact: the payoff beat direction with its promise-match stated
workflow.gate: the payoff answers the exact hook promise and is legible muted

workflow.description: For hard loops: match last-frame composition/motion/lighting to frame one and end on continuing motion (audio looping if used); for open loops: close the payoff, then open the next gap with its numbered marker per the cliffhanger node's integrity rules
workflow.artifact: the seam design or the cliffhanger beat with its continuation reference
workflow.gate: looped: two consecutive plays show no detectable restart; open: payoff delivered and continuation slot confirmed

workflow.action: Run the muted watch-through and the tension-line check
workflow.description: Review the full plan with sound off: hook promise, escalation raises, tension carrier (at least one visual), and payoff must all land; confirm the tension line releases exactly on the payoff
workflow.artifact: a silent-pass checklist with the tension line drawn (carrier, start, rise, release)
workflow.gate: the complete story reads muted and the release coincides with the payoff beat

priority_rationale: The evidence base, the clip-beat frame, and the muted-autoplay gate come first because every downstream decision — hook, ladder, payoff, ending — is either justified by the retention evidence, budgeted by the beat mapping, or constrained by silent legibility; hook and structure nodes precede the ending nodes they feed, and the series-level nodes come last because they amortize per-reel doctrine that must exist before it can be templated.

dominance_rules.rule: When an engagement statistic and its honesty tag travel separately, the tag wins: the claim is restated at its tagged strength or removed
dominance_rules.rationale: the KB's authority rests on never presenting attribution-grade or lore-grade numbers as measured fact
dominance_rules.trigger: any retention/sharing/sound figure appears without its FACT / FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE tag
dominance_rules.action: re-tag from the grounding file or strike the figure; the load-bearing qualitative conclusion is kept

dominance_rules.rule: When hook arrest and setup grounding compete for the opening seconds, the hook wins unconditionally
dominance_rules.rationale: the retention cliff is winner-take-all — grounding a story nobody stays for is worthless
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan spends the first 1-2 seconds on orientation, logo, or establishing material
dominance_rules.action: move the arresting frame to position one; setup inherits and compresses into the remainder of clips 1-2

dominance_rules.rule: When silent legibility and audio-carried meaning conflict, the muted viewer wins
dominance_rules.rationale: the majority first exposure is muted (2016 publisher-reported ~85%, and autoplay-muted regardless), so audio may enhance but never carry
dominance_rules.trigger: any beat — especially the payoff — whose content exists only in the audio track
dominance_rules.action: add the visual or text carrier for that beat; keep the audio version as the sound-on bonus

dominance_rules.rule: When a hard loop and a felt dead-stop release pull against each other, the ending mode decided at planning time wins
dominance_rules.rationale: retrofitting either ending is rework — the loop constrains frame one, the stop constrains the seam
dominance_rules.trigger: an edit-stage proposal to change the ending mode after clips exist
dominance_rules.action: keep the planned mode; log the impulse as input to the format's next instance instead

dominance_rules.rule: When the payoff and any earlier clip compete for the biggest raise, the payoff wins
dominance_rules.rationale: a mid-ladder peak makes the ending an anticlimax and kills rewatch, share, and loop value
dominance_rules.trigger: the ladder plan shows a mid-reel raise exceeding the final clip
dominance_rules.action: demote or resequence the middle raise, or upgrade the payoff clip until it tops the ladder

dominance_rules.rule: When a series-arc role and standalone-reel discipline conflict, the standalone reel wins
dominance_rules.rationale: feed distribution delivers posts to mostly cold, unordered viewers; a series beat that fails cold is a failed post whatever it does for the arc
dominance_rules.trigger: a reel plan leans on prior posts for its hook to make sense or its payoff to land
dominance_rules.action: rework the reel to pass cold-viewer hook/payoff checks; carry the series meaning as an optional layer for followers

dominance_rules.rule: When the quiet-luxury register and a louder attention tactic conflict, the register wins unless the frame is illegible
dominance_rules.rationale: the persona's value is the patrician quiet-luxury position; loud tactics buy one reel's attention at the brand's expense
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed hook or text layer uses flash, prominent logos, or shouting typography
dominance_rules.action: restyle within the register; only if the muted frame cannot name the world does a restrained text layer get added

dominance_rules.rule: When craft doctrine and this account's measured data disagree, the data wins for this account
dominance_rules.rationale: every structure rule here is tagged ESTIMATE / craft doctrine — a prior, not a law; account-level evidence outranks priors at equal scope
dominance_rules.trigger: retention/share/replay data contradicts a doctrine rule (e.g., a slow-build format outperforming arrest-first)
dominance_rules.action: adopt the data-backed variant for the affected format, update the node's confidence, and keep the doctrine as default elsewhere

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the ending mode before composing the hook
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reshooting frame one because a hard loop chosen in the edit needs a return composition the hook never planned for

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm a continuation slot before publishing any open-loop ending
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the account-scale clickbait cleanup — apology posts, caption edits, and trust repair after a part-2 promise nobody scheduled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the hook promise and the payoff beat as one contract in the same planning pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at review that the reel pays off a different promise than it opened, forcing a new hook or a new final clip

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the clip-beat budget before prompting any clip
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generating beautiful clips that have no beat slot — the overstuffed plan trimmed by discarding paid-for material

anti_rework_rules.rule: Plan the escalation ladder as an ordered list with the top rung reserved for the payoff
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mid-production discovery that the biggest raise was spent in clip three, requiring a new, larger payoff clip

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the muted watch-through on the plan, not the finished edit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-editing or re-generating clips because a spoken payoff or audio-only tension carrier was caught after assembly

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every borrowed statistic at import time with its grounding-file honesty tag
anti_rework_rules.prevents: walking back published claims (and re-briefing stakeholders) when an unaudited figure is challenged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the payoff's frame-one returnability before committing a format instance to the hard loop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: seam surgery on a one-way reveal — the teleport-cut fix that either breaks the loop or forces a reshoot

iteration_protocol.trigger: post-publish retention shows a first-3-seconds drop steeper than the account's norm
iteration_protocol.action: audit the hook against the construction rules (motion in frame one, arresting open, front-loaded promise, glance-legible register) and re-plan the format's hook template

iteration_protocol.trigger: retention sags mid-reel while the hook holds
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the escalation ladder: find the holding rungs, add a second raise axis or shorten the reel; verify a visual tension carrier spans the middle

iteration_protocol.trigger: viewers reach the final clip but replay, share, or follow rates disappoint
iteration_protocol.action: audit the promise-match and the ending: does the payoff fill the hook's gap at the ladder's top, and is the ending mode aligned with the format goal

iteration_protocol.trigger: comment sentiment flags baiting or a broken part-2 promise
iteration_protocol.action: invoke the open-loop integrity rules: close outstanding loops cheaply, resize future gaps to their fills, and tighten the continuation-slot gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a looped reel shows a detectable seam or loop replays fail to materialize in the data
iteration_protocol.action: re-engineer the seam (composition/motion/lighting match, continuing motion) or reassign the format's default ending to open/plain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format's performance decays across repeated instances
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the format's raise content, rotate it out of the grid, or replace it; check that the template did not override standalone reel checks

iteration_protocol.trigger: new primary evidence surfaces (a retrievable Facebook IQ page, fresh Mosseri statements, a short-video sharing or sound-on study)
iteration_protocol.action: re-tag the affected claims, update the evidence sheet, and propagate strength changes to every rule that cited the old tags
